title: Applied Econometrics I: Regression Analysis for Causal Inference
officialDescription: Provides a rigorous foundation in applied econometrics with a focus on regression analysis for causal inference. Regression analysis helps address real-world problems beyond prediction, offering tools to examine causal relationships. Emphasizes both theoretical foundations—model assumptions, derivations, and identification strategies—and hands-on empirical data analysis. By the end of the course, students will be able to frame testable hypotheses, analyze complex real-world data, and apply econometric methods to inform research, policy, and data-driven business strategies.
studentDescription: Study regression, causal inference, and empirical evidence using econometric methods.
sourceNotes: The MSDS page lists this as Applied Econometrics I. The official catalog title, Applied Econometrics I: Regression Analysis for Causal Inference, is preserved here.

title: Introduction to Biostatistics
officialDescription: Rates and proportions, sensitivity, specificity, two-way tables, odds ratios, relative risk, ordered and non-ordered classifications, rends, case-control studies, elements of regression including logistic and Poisson, additivity and interaction, combination of studies and meta-analysis.
studentDescription: Analyze rates, proportions, risk, and regression models commonly used in health studies.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Biostatistics, others with permission.

title: Algorithms and Complexity
officialDescription: Design and analysis of efficient computer algorithms. Algorithm design techniques, including divide-and-conquer, depth-first search, and greedy approaches. Worst-case and average-case analysis. Models of computation. NP-complete problems.
studentDescription: Build algorithm-design and complexity-analysis foundations for efficient computation.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to grad students in CSE, others with consent. Recommended preparation: Discrete math; fluency in a high-level programming language; data structures, algorithms at the level of CSE 2050. Students cannot receive credit for both CSE 3500 and 5050.

title: Discrete Optimization
officialDescription: Methods and techniques used to solve combinatorial optimization problems with examples drawn from industry such as scheduling, resource allocation, and routing. Features a mix of theory and practice using state-of-the-art tools to solve classic problems.
studentDescription: Use combinatorial optimization to address scheduling, resource allocation, and routing problems.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent. Recommended preparation: CSE 3500 and MATH 2210Q.

title: Big Data Analytics
officialDescription: Focuses on data science and big data analytics. Introduces basic concepts of data science and analytics. Different algorithmic techniques employed to process data will be discussed. Specific topics include: Parallel and out-of-core algorithms and data structures, Rules mining, Clustering algorithms, Text mining, String algorithms, Data reduction techniques, and Learning algorithms. Applications such as motif search, k-locus association, k-mer counting, error correction, sequence assembly, genotype-phenotype correlations, etc. will be investigated.
studentDescription: Explore algorithms and data-processing techniques for large-scale analytical problems.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent. Recommended preparation: CSE 3500 and MATH 2210Q.

title: Bioinformatics
officialDescription: Advanced mathematical models and computational techniques in bioinformatics. Topics covered include genome mapping and sequencing, sequence alignment, database search, gene prediction, genome rearrangements, phylogenetic trees, and computational proteomics.
studentDescription: Apply mathematical models and computation to biological sequence and genome problems.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent.

title: Bayesian Machine Learning
officialDescription: Bayesian machine learning is a unifying methodology for reasoning about uncertainty when modelling complex data. This course begins by covering the foundations of probabilistic modelling, Monte Carlo and variational inference algorithms, and model checking. We build on these foundations by considering essential models, e.g., mixed-membership and hierarchical models, and their applications. The course concludes with a survey of recent advances in Bayesian machine learning focusing on Bayesian nonparametrics and other advanced topics.
studentDescription: Use probabilistic models and Bayesian computation to reason about uncertainty in complex data.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Department consent required; open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with permission. Recommended preparation: CSE3500; MATH 2110, 3160 or STAT 3345Q, or the equivalent; CSE 4820 or 5819 are also desirable but not as critical.

title: Probabilistic Graphical Models
officialDescription: Probabilistic graphical models provide a flexible framework for analyzing large, complex, heterogeneous, and noisy data. They are the basis for state-of-the-art analysis methods in a wide variety of application domains, from autonomous robotics and computer vision to medical diagnosis and social networks. This course covers (a) representation, including Bayesian and Markov networks, (b) inference, both exact and approximate, and (c) estimation of both parameters and structure of graphical models.
studentDescription: Represent complex relationships with graphical models and learn methods for inference and estimation.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Department consent required; open to graduate students in the Computer Science and Engineering program, others with permission.

title: Introduction to Cyber-Security
officialDescription: Introductory to the area of cyber-security. The course focuses on applied cryptography, and some of its applications and related areas in cyber security, including network and web security, usable security, privacy/anonymity, and block-chains. The course is systems-oriented; we will discuss many practical vulnerabilities, attacks and defenses. However, esp. in the beginning, we will also learn some theory - mainly, few definitions, and (fewer) proofs.
studentDescription: Explore applied cryptography, practical security vulnerabilities, privacy, and defenses.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Department consent; open to graduate students in the Computer Science and Engineering program, others with permission. Not open for credit to students who have passed CSE 3400. Recommended preparation: CSE 2500.

title: Text Analytics
officialDescription: This course provides an applied introduction to text analytics with special emphasis on its application to education. Students will learn to use common toolkits in the Python ecosystem to analyze large-scale text data in order to generate insights into educational, cognitive, and social processes.
studentDescription: Use Python tools to analyze large-scale text data, with applications in education and social processes.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: EPSY 5641. Recommended preparation: This course requires an understanding of introductory statistics and regression at the level of EPSY 5605 and EPSY 5610 as well as some prior experience with statistical programming in a language like R or Python.

title: Special Topics in Graduate Education
studentDescription: MSDS lists an Applied Generative AI topic under this special-topics code. Confirm the specific topic, credits, preparation, and availability with the program.
sourceNotes: The MSDS page lists Applied Generative AI under GRAD 5900. The official catalog entry is Special Topics in Graduate Education with variable credits and no topic-specific description or prerequisites. Confirm the intended topic and preparation with the program.

title: Marketing Management
officialDescription: Introduction to key marketing concepts of interest to all business managers. Students learn to think strategically about customers and competition and develop an understanding of how firms manage products, prices, channels and promotions in an integrated manner. Students gain experience identifying opportunities and threats in the market environment, and making segmenting, targeting, and positioning decisions.
studentDescription: Connect market analysis, forecasting, segmentation, and marketing strategy to business decisions.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to MBA, M.S. in Social Responsibility and Impact in Business, MSBAPM, MS in Supply Chain Management, and MS Data Science students, others with consent. Not open to students who have passed MKTG 5182.

title: Introduction to Geospatial Analysis with Remote Sensing
officialDescription: Introduction to collecting, managing, displaying, and analyzing geospatial data. Topics include coordinate systems, finding and using existing sources of geospatial data, analysis of vector and raster data, creating geospatial data with remote sensing, concepts of Global Positioning System (GPS), topographic and landscape analyses, and spatial interpolation.
studentDescription: Build a practical foundation for collecting, managing, and analyzing geospatial data and remote sensing.

title: Remote Sensing of the Environment
officialDescription: Introduction to remote sensing theory and practice. Includes electromagnetic radiation, spectral reflectance, earth observation platforms and sensors, image processing methods, and multidisciplinary applications.
studentDescription: Understand remote-sensing theory, sensors, image processing, and environmental applications.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Instructor consent.

title: Python Scripting for Geospatial Analysis
officialDescription: GIS scripting techniques in Python for geospatial analyses, enabling students to pursue integrated research in earth resources data geoprocessing applications.
studentDescription: Use Python scripting to automate geospatial analyses and earth-resources data processing.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Instructor consent. Recommended preparation: NRE 5215 or equivalent.

title: Introduction to Deep Learning
officialDescription: Introduction to topics related to deep learning and will build on your previous experience in predictive analytics. Use of neural networks for a host of data and applications - including time series data, text data, geospatial data, and image data.
studentDescription: Apply neural networks to data including time series, text, geospatial information, and images.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5604 (if OPIM 5604 was completed before Fall 2025, prior knowledge of Python programming is required); open only to MBA, MSBAPM, and MS FinTech students, others with consent.

title: Advanced Deep Learning
officialDescription: This course covers advanced AI models, including Bayesian Neural Networks, Graph Neural Networks, and Transformers. Students will gain hands-on experience implementing and evaluating these models using PyTorch, Keras and other software, with a focus on uncertainty quantification and explainable AI. Practical applications include tabular, time-series, and image data.
studentDescription: Work with advanced neural models, including graphs and transformers, with attention to uncertainty and explainability.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5604 and OPIM 5509; open only to MBA, MSBAPM, and MS FinTech students, others with consent.

title: Data Science using Python
officialDescription: Data science concepts using the Python programming language. Data wrangling and management using Pandas; visualization using MatPlotLib; fundamentals of matrix algebra and regression, with illustrations using Numpy; machine learning, focusing on fundamental concepts, classification, and information extraction.
studentDescription: Use Python for data preparation, visualization, regression, and machine-learning concepts.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5604; MBA, MSBAPM, MS in Supply Chain Management, and MS FinTech students, others with consent. Not open to students who have passed OPIM 5894 when offered as Data Science with Python.
sourceNotes: The MSDS page lists this as Data Science Using Python. The official catalog title, Data Science using Python, is preserved here.

title: Predictive Modeling
officialDescription: Introduces the techniques of predictive modeling in a data-rich business environment. Covers the process of formulating business objectives, data selection, preparation, and partition to successfully design, build, evaluate and implement predictive models for a variety of practical business applications. Predictive models such as neural networks, decision trees, Bayesian classification, and others will be studied. The course emphasizes the relationship of each step to a company's specific business needs, goals and objectives. The focus on the business goal highlights how the process is both powerful and practical.
studentDescription: Build and evaluate predictive models while connecting each analytical step to a business objective.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM Python Bootcamp; Open only to MBA, MSBAPM, MS in Supply Chain Management, and MS FinTech students, others with consent. Corequisite: OPIM 5603.

title: Applied Time Series
officialDescription: Introduction to prediction using time-series regression methods with non-seasonal and seasonal data. Smoothing methods for forecasting. Modeling and forecasting using univariate autoregressive moving average models.
studentDescription: Model time-dependent data and develop forecasting approaches for seasonal and nonseasonal series.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Statistics, others with permission.

title: Applied Spatio-Temporal Statistics
officialDescription: Applied statistical methodology and computing for spatio-temporal data, including visualization, models, and inferences. Extreme value analysis in spatio-temporal contexts. Focus on models that account for spatio-temporal dependence and inferences that provide appropriate uncertainty measures, with applications to real-world problems using open-source software.
studentDescription: Analyze spatial and temporal dependence with models, computing, visualization, and uncertainty assessment.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Statistics, others with permission. Recommended preparation: STAT 5405 or 5605 or GSCU 5400 or 5410 or ERTH 5150 or equivalent.

title: Climate Economics
officialDescription: Analysis of the interactive relationship between the economy and climate change. Use of advanced principles and tools of economics to focus on the costs of changes in the severity and frequency of weather events, how these costs are influenced by markets and policies, and how costs and benefits are distributed across populations within the U.S and across the globe in the short and long terms. Examination of household, firm-level, national and international decision-making as influenced by climate change, taking into account uncertainty, diverging interests, external costs, and evaluation of models used to alternative scenarios.
studentDescription: Use economic tools to examine climate impacts, uncertainty, policy, and how costs and benefits are distributed.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: This course and ARE 3438E may not both be taken for credit.

title: Environmental and Resource Economics
officialDescription: Natural resource use and environmental quality analysis using economic theory. Reviews of empirical research and relevant policy issues.
studentDescription: Analyze natural-resource use and environmental quality through economic theory and policy evidence.

title: Valuing the Environment
officialDescription: Conceptual and practical understanding of main methods used to evaluate economic benefits of environmental protection and damages from degradation. Methods include: change in productivity, hedonic pricing, travel cost method, contingent valuation, defensive expenditures, replacement costs, and cost-of-illness. Topics covered include: recreation, soil-erosion, energy, forestry, hazardous waste, air pollution, deforestation, wetlands, wildlife, biodiversity, noise, visibility, water, and water pollution. Taught together with ARE 4438E.
studentDescription: Explore methods for valuing environmental protection and assessing damage from degradation.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: ARE 1150 or ECON 1200 or ECON 1201 or equivalent with instructor's consent. Students who have taken ARE 4438E cannot take ARE 5538 for credit.

title: Categorical Data Analysis
officialDescription: Statistical analysis of data on a nominal scale: discrete distributions, contingency tables, odds ratios, interval estimates, goodness of fit tests, logistic/probit/complementary log-log regression, Poisson-related regression.
studentDescription: Model categorical outcomes, contingency tables, and odds using statistical methods for discrete data.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: BIST 5505 and 5605; or instructor consent.

title: Concepts and Analysis of Survival Data
officialDescription: Survival models, censoring and truncation, nonparametric estimation of survival functions, comparison of treatment groups, mathematical and graphical methods for assessing goodness of fit, parametric and nonparametric regression models.
studentDescription: Analyze time-to-event data with survival models, censoring, group comparisons, and regression.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Biostatistics, others with permission.

title: Longitudinal Data Analysis
officialDescription: Statistical theory and methodology for data collected over time in a clustered manner: design of experiments, exploratory data analysis, linear models for continuous data, general linear models for discrete data, marginal and mixed models, treatment of missing data.
studentDescription: Analyze repeated and clustered observations with marginal and mixed models and attention to missing data.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: BIST 5505 and 5605; or instructor consent.

title: Performance Engineering
officialDescription: Study of performance engineering techniques for the development of software systems to meet performance objectives. Software performance principles, hierarchical performance modeling, and current research trends related to Software Performance Engineering. Methods for computer performance evaluation and analysis with emphasis on direct measurement and analytic modeling, including queuing networks, computation structure models, state charts, probabilistic languages, and Petri-nets. Case studies for the evaluation and analysis of software architecture and design alternatives.
studentDescription: Use performance modeling and measurement to evaluate software-system design alternatives.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent. Recommended preparation: CSE 3504 and 4500 or the equivalent.

title: High-Performance Parallel Computing
officialDescription: Topics in high-performance computing such as the following (1) Parallel Algorithms and Parallel Computation: including programming models (Circuits and PRAMs), complexity analysis, modern parallel platforms and programming libraries; (2) Shared- and Distributed-Memory Parallel Architectures: including cache coherence, Memory consistency, processor synchronization, latency tolerance and hiding; (3) Interconnection Networks: including quantitative measures, topologies, switch architectures, routing strategies; as well as (4) Contemporary and Future HPC Systems.
studentDescription: Explore parallel algorithms, architectures, libraries, and high-performance computing systems.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent. Recommended preparation: CSE 4302 and 4500.

title: Algorithms
officialDescription: Introduction to the design and analysis of algorithms. The course will discuss fundamental design techniques and related issues such as amortized analysis, linear programming, network flow, NP-Completeness, approximation algorithms, randomized algorithms, advanced data structures, and parallel algorithms.
studentDescription: Deepen algorithm design and analysis through optimization, randomized approaches, and advanced data structures.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent. Recommended preparation: CSE 3500 or the equivalent.

title: Computational Complexity
studentDescription: The MSDS specialty list describes computational complexity and resource-bounded computation. Current catalog metadata needs program verification.
sourceNotes: Verified on the MSDS specialty list, but absent from the current departmental Graduate Catalog. Official title, credits, and enrollment requirements need program confirmation. No current offering is inferred.

title: Distributed Computing and Fault Tolerance
studentDescription: The MSDS specialty list describes robust distributed algorithms and fault tolerance. Current catalog metadata needs program verification.
sourceNotes: Verified on the MSDS specialty list, but absent from the current departmental Graduate Catalog. Official title, credits, and enrollment requirements need program confirmation. No current offering is inferred.

title: Introduction to Quantum Computing
officialDescription: Introduction to quantum computing, quantum algorithms, and quantum information theory. Quantum mechanics including elementary aspects of its mathematical formalism; quantum circuit model and quantum complexity theory; development and analysis of several fundamental quantum algorithms, focusing on Grover's algorithm for database search and Shor's number-theoretic algorithms. Second half covers the density matrix formalism of quantum mechanics, von Neumann entropy, quantum channels, and quantum error-correction. If time permits, some implementations of quantum computers and current progress will be discussed.
studentDescription: Explore quantum computation, algorithms, information theory, and error correction.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent. Recommended preparation: CSE 3500, CSE 3502, and MATH 2420Q.

title: Data Visualization and Communication
officialDescription: This course will focus on fundamental theory and practice of data visualization and communication. Topics to be covered include different data types, algorithms for data visualization, design of effective visualization for analysis and communication, exploratory and explanatory data analysis (for discovery of new information, detecting flaws, etc.), using data visualization to convey different messages, existing tools for data visualization, and making presentations with data. Several case studies, such as engineering, economics, or health, will be discussed.
studentDescription: Study visualization theory and practice for exploration, explanation, and presentation of data.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Only open to Computer Science and Engineering graduate students, others with permission. Recommended preparation: knowledge of algorithms, some programming experience required.

title: Machine Learning for Physical Sciences and Systems
officialDescription: (Also offered as SE 5602.) Foundational knowledge in applied aspects of machine learning, including methods for handling uncertain, small, and imbalanced data; feature selection and representation learning; and model selection and assessment. Students will also gain exposure to state-of-the-art research on interpretability of machine learning models, stability of machine learning algorithms, and meta-learning. Topics will be discussed in the context of recent advances in machine learning for materials, chemistry, and physics applications, with an emphasis on the unique opportunities and challenges at the intersection of machine learning and these fields.
studentDescription: Connect machine-learning methods to physical-science and systems applications.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Computer Science and Engineering, MEng in Advanced Systems Engineering, and MEng in Data Science, others with department consent. Recommended prep: Basic concepts in machine learning, linear algebra, optimization, statistics.

title: Systems Biology: Constructing Biological Knowledgebase
studentDescription: The MSDS specialty list describes systems biology and biological knowledge bases. Current catalog metadata needs program verification.
sourceNotes: Verified on the MSDS specialty list, but absent from the current departmental Graduate Catalog. Official title, credits, and enrollment requirements need program confirmation. No current offering is inferred.

title: Reinforcement Learning
officialDescription: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a powerful paradigm for autonomous systems to learn to make decisions, and it is relevant to an enormous range of tasks, including robotics, game playing, consumer modeling and healthcare. This class will provide a solid introduction to the field of reinforcement learning and students will learn about the core concepts, design principles, widely used algorithms, RL with functional approximation, and generalization of RL. Through a combination of lectures, literature review, and written and coding assignments, students will become well versed in key ideas and techniques for RL including basics of reinforcement learning as well as deep reinforcement learning — an area that combines deep learning techniques with reinforcement learning.
studentDescription: Study reinforcement learning, including decision-making algorithms and deep reinforcement learning.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: CSE 4820 or CSE 5819; open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent. Recommended preparation: CSE 3500, MATH 2110Q, MATH 2210Q, and MATH 3160 or the equivalent.

title: String Algorithms and Applications in Bioinformatics
studentDescription: The MSDS specialty list describes string algorithms for bioinformatics applications. Current catalog metadata needs program verification.
sourceNotes: Verified on the MSDS specialty list, but absent from the current departmental Graduate Catalog. Official title, credits, and enrollment requirements need program confirmation. No current offering is inferred.

title: Modern Cryptography: Foundations
officialDescription: The foundations of modern cryptography introducing basic topics such as one-way functions, pseudorandom generators, and computational hardness assumptions based on number theory. Fundamental cryptographic constructions such as hard-core predicates, secure symmetric encryption and message-authentication codes, and public-key cryptography.
studentDescription: Study foundational concepts and mathematical tools behind modern cryptography.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent. Recommended preparation: MATH 3160, CSE 3500, and CSE 3502 or the equivalent.

title: Modern Cryptography: Primitives and Protocols
officialDescription: Modern cryptography, emphasizing provable security and concrete constructions based on the hardness of specific computational problems. After surveying some basic cryptographic primitives and associated number-theoretic constructions, focuses on public-key infrastructure and protocols: it will cover such topics as digital signatures, identification and key-exchange schemes, distributed key generation, blind signatures, zero-knowledge proofs, and private function computation.
studentDescription: Explore cryptographic primitives, protocols, and their security properties.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent. Recommended preparation: MATH 3160, CSE 3500, CSE 3502, and CSE 4702 or the equivalent.

title: Computational Problems in Evolutionary Genomics
officialDescription: Computational and algorithmic approaches for problems arising in evolutionary genomics. Topics may include phylogenetic trees inference, population evolutionary models and theory, understanding complex evolutionary processes and other related topics. Both combinatorial optimization and stochastic approaches will be covered.
studentDescription: Use computational methods to investigate evolutionary-genomics problems.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: CSE 5800; open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent.

title: Randomization in Computing
officialDescription: Introduction to the theory and practice of randomization and randomized algorithms as a technique for science and engineering problem solving. Topics to be covered include: probability theory, types of randomization, sorting and selection, hashing and skip list, finger-printing, packet routing, geometry and linear programming, graph algorithms, combinatorial optimization, and external memory algorithms.
studentDescription: Study randomized computation and probabilistic methods in algorithm design.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: CSE 5500. Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent.

title: Computational Genomics
officialDescription: Advanced computational methods for genomic data analysis. Topics covered include motif finding, gene expression analysis, regulatory network inference, comparative genomics, genomic sequence variation and linkage analysis.
studentDescription: Explore computational approaches to genomic analysis.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: CSE 5800 or BME 5800. Open to graduate students in the CSE program, others with consent.

title: Fundamentals of Ecological Modeling
officialDescription: Quantitative inference from ecological and environmental data. Choosing modeling methods based on knowledge of biological processes. Frequentist and Bayesian approaches; analysis of real and simulated data sets.
studentDescription: Build and assess ecological models for biological and environmental questions.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: STAT 1000Q or 1100Q or 3445 or 5005 or 5505; or equivalent with instructor consent.

title: Phylogenetics
officialDescription: Estimation of genealogies at the level of species and above, and their application and relevance to systematics, population genetics, molecular evolution, and comparative biology. Emphasizes maximum likelihood and Bayesian approaches. Laboratory provides practical experience with modern phylogenetics software.
studentDescription: Study methods for reconstructing evolutionary relationships and analyzing phylogenetic evidence.

title: Hierarchical Linear Modeling
officialDescription: Theory and applications of hierarchical linear modeling, including organizational and longitudinal multilevel models.
studentDescription: Analyze nested data with hierarchical linear models.

title: Structural Equation Modeling
officialDescription: An introduction to structural equation modeling. Develop, modify, and interpret a variety of structural equation models commonly used in social science research. Linear models with only observed variables (path analysis), latent variable models without causal paths (confirmatory factor analysis), and latent variable models with causal paths (structural equation modeling). Conceptual understanding, application, and interpretation of structural equation models.
studentDescription: Model relationships among observed and latent variables using structural equation methods.

title: Big Data and Strategic Marketing
studentDescription: The MSDS specialty list describes analytical tools for strategic marketing and large datasets. Current catalog metadata needs program verification.
sourceNotes: Verified on the MSDS specialty list, but absent from the current departmental Graduate Catalog. Official title, credits, and enrollment requirements need program confirmation. No current offering is inferred.

title: Marketing Research and Intelligence
officialDescription: This course provides a framework and tools for obtaining and using data to gain marketing insights. Students learn to identify the most appropriate quantitative and qualitative research techniques to answer particular marketing questions, design studies for maximum insight, identify and apply appropriate methods to collect and analyze data, and communicate findings to aid managerial decision making. Students gain practice conducting research, analyzing data, and reporting findings.
studentDescription: Design marketing research and interpret qualitative and quantitative evidence about customers and markets.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to MBA and MSBAPM students, others with consent.

title: Marketing and Digital Analytics
officialDescription: This course provides an understanding of how marketing and digital analytics can be used to gain insights and make marketing decisions. Students learn how to use analytics to discover customer needs, satisfy customer preferences, predict customer behavior, and allocate media and communication resources. Students gain hands-on experience designing, conducting, and communicating results of analytics initiatives.
studentDescription: Translate marketing data into insights about customer needs, behavior, and resource allocation.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to MBA, M.S. in Social Responsibility and Impact in Business, and MS BAPM students, others with consent.

title: Pricing and Revenue Management
officialDescription: This course provides an overview of pricing strategies and tactics to achieve revenue management goals. Students learn how to develop pricing strategies to account for temporal changes in customer demands, differences across customer segments, loyalty programs, product inventory, and price-quality relationships. Students gain experience using analytic tools for revenue management.
studentDescription: Use analytical tools to develop pricing strategies and support revenue-management decisions.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: MKTG 5115, or MKTG 5181 and MKTG 5182.

title: Remote Sensing Image Processing
officialDescription: A variety of related topics that include the physical processes involved in remote sensing and various image processing methods. The labs will be primarily focused on how to use image processing software (e.g., ENVI) to analyze satellite imagery.
studentDescription: Use remote-sensing image-processing methods and software to analyze satellite imagery.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: A course in remote sensing of the environment.

title: Big Data Analytics with Cloud Computing
officialDescription: In-depth, hands-on exploration of various cutting-edge information technologies used for big data analytics. The first half focuses on using big data management techniques for ETL (extract-transform-load) operations. The second half focuses on using big data analytics tools for data mining algorithms such as classification, clustering, and collaborative filtering. Extremely hands-on, requiring students to spend significant time working with large datasets. Students are expected to have taken at least one course in data modeling and one course in data mining (please see pre-requisites) or have significant related work experience. Students should expect to become familiar with the Unix operating system, as well as data programming concepts. Students may be required to install some software on their computers on their own, with very little support, if any, from the instructor or anyone else. Students should be willing to troubleshoot any issues during installation, drawing help from Google searches.
studentDescription: Use cloud and big-data tools for data management, processing, and analytical workflows.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5604 or BADM 5604; and OPIM 5272.

title: Adaptive Business Intelligence
officialDescription: The use of techniques from statistics and optimization to implement adaptive business intelligence (ABI) decision support systems. The course will introduce students to the different components of ABI systems as well as to the fundamentals of adaptive statistical methods, simulation adaptive methods, and evolutionary algorithms. Applications to diverse management contexts evolving in time will also be discussed.
studentDescription: Combine statistical and optimization techniques in adaptive business decision-support systems.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5603; open only to MBA and MSBAPM students, others with consent.

title: Healthcare Analytics and Research Methods
officialDescription: Evidence-based practice, research techniques, health data collection devices, legislation and regulation of health data, ethical use of health data, and reporting tools. Prepares students for employment opportunities within a clinical or medical research environment.
studentDescription: Explore health-data collection, research methods, regulation, ethics, and reporting.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: BADM 5103 or BADM 5180 or OPIM 5103 or OPIM 5603; open only to MBA and MSBAPM students, others with consent.

title: Web Analytics
officialDescription: Introduction to key concepts, techniques, and tools for analyzing web data to derive actionable customer intelligence, develop digital marketing strategies and evaluate their impacts. Clickstream tracking, search engine analytics, digital experiments, and social analytics.
studentDescription: Use web, clickstream, search, and social-analytics data to evaluate customer behavior and digital strategy.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5604; open only to MBA and MSBAPM students, others with consent.

title: Survival Analysis with SAS
officialDescription: Describes the various methods used for modeling and evaluating survival data, also called time-to-event data. General statistical concepts and techniques, including survival and hazard functions, Kaplan-Meier graphs, log-rank, and related tests, Cox proportional hazards model, and the extended Cox model for time-varying covariates and non-proportional hazards.
studentDescription: Model and evaluate survival and time-to-event data using SAS.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5604; open only to MBA and MSBAPM students, others with consent.

title: Data Mining and Time Series Forecasting
officialDescription: Discusses data mining, time series forecasting and text mining techniques that can be utilized to effectively sift through large volumes of operational data and extract actionable information and knowledge (meaningful patterns, trends, and anomalies) to help optimize organizational processes and significantly improve bottom lines. The course covers theoretical and practical elements of various data analytics techniques such as natural language processing and advanced time series forecasting, with a focus on hands-on application in different business domains.
studentDescription: Apply data mining, text analysis, and time-series forecasting to operational and business questions.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5604 or BADM 5604; open only to MBA, MSBAPM, MS in Supply Chain Management, and MS FinTech students, others with consent.
sourceNotes: The MSDS page lists this as Data Mining and Business Intelligence. The official catalog title, Data Mining and Time Series Forecasting, is preserved here.

title: Applied Multivariate Analysis
officialDescription: Multivariate normal distributions, inference about a mean vector, comparison of several multivariate means, principal components, factor analysis, canonical correlation analysis, discrimination and classification, cluster analysis.
studentDescription: Analyze multivariate data with dimension reduction, classification, clustering, and related statistical methods.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Statistics, others with permission.

title: Bayesian Data Analysis
officialDescription: Theory of statistical inference based on Bayes' Theorem: basic probability theory, linear/nonlinear, graphical, and hierarchical models, decision theory, Bayes estimation and hypothesis testing, prior elicitation, Gibbs sampling, the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, Monte Carlo integration.
studentDescription: Develop Bayesian models and computational methods for inference, decisions, and uncertainty.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: STAT 5585 and 5685; or instructor consent.
